title: A House for the Bell
premise: Folklorist Hazel Thackeray returns to the village of Marrow Fen to record a lullaby that locals will sing only once, and discovers the song is a counting rhyme — one verse for each member of a household the frost claims. When every mirror in Hazel's rented house begins reflecting reality one second late, they realize the house is rehearsing their death and the deaths of the found family gathered under its roof: landlady Bess, her mute grandson Tam, and Hazel's estranged sister Wren. The mirrors' delay shortens nightly, counting down to the frost's final pattern on the glass. To survive, Hazel must teach the family to sing the lullaby out of order — breaking the count — while offering the house a memory in exchange: their own twelve years of rationalizing away the noises. In the end the family escapes into a snowless dawn, but Hazel stays behind as the house's new keeper of songs, remembered by no one except a single recording that plays back a voice no one recognizes.
about_author: Petra Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist of oral histories who spent a decade collecting funeral songs across northern England before turning to fiction. They write horror about houses that remember more kindly than people do.

chapters.title: The Song They Sing Once
chapters.summary: Hazel arrives in Marrow Fen to record the lullaby from Bess, who sings it once and refuses to repeat it, hands shaking. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity; the reader senses the village's fear before Hazel does.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Settling into the rented house, Hazel catalogs its noises — pipes, settling beams, wind — with practiced rationality, while bonding with Bess's grandson Tam, who communicates through drawings of a figure made of frost. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: tenderness undercut by dread; the explanations begin to feel like rituals.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Wren arrives uninvited, hoping to reconcile, just as Hazel notices the bathroom mirror reflecting the room a beat behind. Testing it with a dropped cup, Hazel watches the reflection shatter before the real cup lands. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: vertigo; the rational framework cracks for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Frost Draws
chapters.summary: Fern patterns spread across every window overnight, each one matching a drawing Tam has hidden under his mattress — drawings dated years before his birth. Bess admits the house took her husband and daughter. POV: alternating Hazel and Bess. Emotional beat: grief surfacing as guilt; the count has begun.

chapters.title: Verse by Verse
chapters.summary: Hazel transcribes the lullaby and realizes each verse names a household member in order of claiming; the final verse is blank, waiting. The mirror delay drops to half a second. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: scholarly control curdling into panic as folklore becomes instruction manual.

chapters.title: The House Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Trapped inside by an unnatural blizzard, the family finds rooms rearranged into scenes from their own memories — Hazel's childhood bedroom, Bess's wedding kitchen — each subtly wrong, each colder than the last. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the sisters' old wounds reopen; the house weaponizes love.

chapters.title: Tam Counts Backward
chapters.summary: Tam speaks for the first time in six years, reciting the lullaby backward, revealing he was claimed once already and returned — incomplete. The mirrors now show the room a full second ahead instead of behind. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: heartbreaking hope; the boy who came back knows the way out.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Bess tries to offer herself alone to finish the count and spare the others; the frost accepts her memory instead, leaving her smiling and empty. The family realizes the house doesn't want bodies — it wants the years people spend explaining things away. POV: Bess, then Hazel. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice; survival has always had a price here.

chapters.title: Sung Out of Order
chapters.summary: In the climax, as the frost writes its final pattern across the last mirror, Hazel leads the family in singing the verses shuffled — Wren's verse first, Tam's last, the blank verse filled with Hazel's own name offered freely. The house hesitates, then bargains. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: defiant love against an ancient arithmetic.

chapters.title: A Voice No One Knows
chapters.summary: Dawn comes snowless. Wren, Tam, and the emptied-but-breathing Bess walk out; Hazel remains as keeper, trading their memories for the family's freedom. Weeks later, Wren plays Hazel's field recordings and hears a stranger's voice singing a song she almost remembers. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — found family saved, at the cost of being forgotten by it.
